In the context of cars, AUV stands for **Asian Utility Vehicle** [d1][d5]. The term is a coined label for a category of vehicles predominantly sold in Asia, particularly in developing Asian countries, designed to seat 8–10 people, haul goods, and serve commercial purposes [d5]. First seen on the road in the late 1960s and early 1970s, AUVs are also known as Basic Utility Vehicles (BUVs) [d1]. Some of the earliest examples in the Philippines include the Toyota Tamaraw, the Ford Tiera series, and the GM Harabas — vehicles primarily used for carrying the maximum number of passengers [d2]. Over time, the AUV category evolved into wagon-type vehicles such as the Toyota FX (later Revo) and the Crosswind [d5], and the distinction between AUVs and MPVs (multi-purpose vehicles) has become increasingly blurred [d2]. Compared to SUVs, AUVs lack significant off-road capability and are simply passenger vehicles not designed for rough terrain [d1][d2].
